prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Engineers who studied the system years later described it, above all, as ______.

worlds.passage: In 1983 a small company released the operating system that would run its office computers for the next decade. It was the first office system to offer windows and a mouse, and rival firms that wanted their programs to run on it had to buy a license; two that worked out its commands on their own were sued. Because only the company knew how its single interlocked program worked, every repair waited for its engineers, and an office could lose a day to one failed disk. Engineers who studied the system years later described it, above all, as ______.
worlds.explanation: The company licensed access, sued imitators, and kept the workings to itself, so engineers called the system "proprietary." "Modular" fails because it was a single interlocked program. "Resilient" fails because one failed disk could cost an office a day, and "outmoded" fails because it was the first to offer windows and a mouse.

modular.why: it was not built from separable parts

resilient.quote: lose a day to one failed disk

outmoded.quote: first office system to offer windows
outmoded.why: it was ahead of its time

worlds.passage: In 1983 a small company released the operating system that would run its office computers for the next decade. It was the first office system to offer windows and a mouse, and its full code was printed in a manual anyone could buy. Offices that needed only word processing installed only that piece, adding a printing or mail piece later, and swapping in a newer version of any piece left the rest untouched, though a fault in one piece still meant restarting the whole machine. Engineers who studied the system years later described it, above all, as ______.
worlds.explanation: Offices could install, add and replace separate pieces independently, so engineers called the system "modular." "Proprietary" fails because its code was printed for anyone to buy. "Resilient" fails because one fault meant restarting the whole machine, and "outmoded" fails because it was the first to offer windows and a mouse.

proprietary.quote: printed in a manual anyone could buy
proprietary.why: its workings were open to all

outmoded.quote: first office system to offer windows
outmoded.why: it was ahead of its time

worlds.passage: In 1983 a small company released the operating system that would run its office computers for the next decade. Its full code was printed in a manual anyone could buy, and it was written as one interlocked program that froze whenever a disk failed. Its screens showed only green text and accepted only typed commands, a design that rival firms had replaced with windows and a mouse two years before it shipped. "Modular" fails because it was one interlocked program, and "resilient" fails because it froze whenever a disk failed.
